question: The difference between the simple interest and compound interest on ₹1,000 for 1 year at 20% per annum, compounded half-yearly, is:
solution:
**Given:**

P=1000, R=20%, T= 1year

**Formula used:**

SI = (P× R× T)/(100)

A = P(1+(R)/(100))^T

P= Principal

R= Rate of interest

T= Time

A = Amount

**Calculation:**

for compounded half-yearly, the rate gets halved and time gets doubled

⇒ R = 20/2

⇒ R = 10%

⇒ T = 1 × 2

⇒ T = 2 years

For SI

⇒ SI = (P× R× T)/(100)

⇒ SI = (1000×10×2)/(100)

⇒ SI = Rs. 200

For CI

⇒ A = P(1+(R)/(100))^T=1000(1+(10)/(100))²

⇒ A = 1000(1+(1)/(10))²

⇒ A = 1000((11)/(10) × (11)/(10))

⇒ A = Rs. 1210

⇒ I = A - P

⇒ I = 1210-1000

 

⇒ I = Rs. 210

Difference = CI - SI

⇒ 210-200

⇒ Rs.10

**∴ The answer is Rs. 10.**
